question: What makes the cognition of nonbeing possible?
premises: Nonbeing can appear as an object of cognition.
Such appearance depends on the operation of time.
The absolute consciousness is perfectly full and contains all forms.
inference: The cognition of nonbeing is possible because the perfectly full consciousness, through time, manifests even absence within itself.
plain_english: There, nonbeing becomes an object of cognition, and that happens through the grace of time; for this perfectly full reality bears the form of all things and the self of all.
